explain.say: Think of doing homework. Your desk holds the books you are using right now. Your cupboard holds all your books, even when you are asleep. A computer has both! Look at the board: RAM on one side and storage on the other.

faq.a: RAM, random access memory, is the fast working memory of a computer. It holds the programs and files in use right now, and it is volatile, which means it loses everything when the power goes off.

faq.q: What is storage on a computer?
faq.a: Storage, like an SSD or a hard drive, keeps your files, apps and photos for a long time, even with the power off. It is bigger but slower than RAM.

faq.q: Why do I need to save my work?
faq.a: While you work, your file lives in RAM, which forgets everything if the power goes off. Saving copies it into storage, which keeps it safe.
asks: Why do I lose work if the computer crashes?

faq.q: What is the difference between RAM and storage?
faq.a: RAM is small, very fast and forgets when switched off; storage is large, slower and remembers. RAM is the desk you work at; storage is the cupboard where things are kept.
asks: Is RAM the same as memory?

faq.q: Does more RAM make a computer faster?
faq.a: More RAM lets a computer keep more apps and files open at once without slowing down, because it does not have to keep swapping things to and from slower storage.
asks: How much RAM do I need?
Why does my computer slow down with many tabs?

facts: RAM is volatile memory: it loses its contents when the power is turned off.
The first commercial hard drive, IBM's 350 disk storage unit of 1956, stored about 3.75 megabytes and was roughly the size of two refrigerators.
